chapter: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
title: Joining the band, first rehearsal and heading to New York
summary: He travelled to Massachusetts with his instruments, heard his arrangements played and was told of the Roseland engagement.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I had then a baritone, a bass clarinet, if you look at any of those early pictures, everybody played those things.

As many as you could get, and "Bring it along." I guess this is the enticement, "Come on, bring them along, play them all," and so forth. Well, I had quite a problem getting up there with my bag and all my instruments and all I was loaded. And I had to change trains.

Anyway, I got up there and they had a rehearsal the next morning and they played the "Blue Room" for me and a couple of other things. You know, it was a thrill. Here are things, you write something down and the guys play it. Well, the improvised parts to it, these were the things I was interested in, and they played over things like that and beyond your expectations, you know, lift the whole thing right up. It was a kick.

So what to do. Then I got together and talked with Horvath and Sure, I'd like to join the band. I'd like to do this and do that, and they gave me for that time fairly good pay, and told me that they were on their way into New York to record. This is the way they did. They switched -- Henderson went out to the Greystone and they would come and sit in the Roseland Ballroom and of course, it was always about a day that they would overlap when they were both playing in each place.
